TESTCASES.TEST: The declared default of an attribute the start tag leaves out is supplied.
A specified value is kept; only the attribute that is left out is defaulted.
A #FIXED declaration supplies its value when the attribute is left out.
#IMPLIED supplies nothing; the default of another attribute is still supplied.
#REQUIRED supplies nothing; the missing attribute breaks the Required Attribute constraint.
A default is supplied to the element type that declares it and to no other.
A default is normalised as a specified value is: references replaced, literal white space to a space, a character reference to a tab kept, a NMTOKENS value collapsed.
Nested elements, and elements that arrive in an entity replacement text, are defaulted.
The first declaration of an attribute is binding, so its default is the one supplied.
The default of an ATTLIST in an external subset that the processor reads is supplied.
An ATTLIST that follows a reference to a parameter entity that was not read is not processed, so no default is supplied.
The same ATTLIST in a standalone document is processed.
An ATTLIST that precedes the unread parameter-entity reference is processed.
standalone="yes" and a default declared in the external subset: the supplied attribute breaks the Standalone Document Declaration constraint.
standalone="yes" and a default declared in the internal subset: valid.
A defaulted xmlns:p declares the prefix, so the document is namespace-well-formed.
The same document with an ordinary default leaves the prefix unbound.
A supplied IDREF value is checked as a specified one is: it names no ID.
xml:lang="" and a language tag are values.
Well-formed BCP 47 tags: language-region, variant, script, private use, grandfathered.
en_GB is not a language tag.
A language subtag is letters.
A tag does not end in a hyphen.
Distinct NCName values.
xml:id needs no declaration to be an ID (a value is normalised first); the DTD-validity constraint on undeclared attributes still applies.
q:r is a Name and not an NCName.
1a is not a Name: an xml:id error, and a violation of the ID constraint.
The same xml:id value twice: an error on each.
Duplicates after normalisation, with no declaration.
An xml:id value equal to the value of an attribute the DTD declares as ID.
xml:id declared with a type other than ID.
LEIRI references: absolute, relative with a space, a non-ASCII letter, a percent escape, a query and a fragment.
A percent sign that does not start two hexadecimal digits.
A colon in the first segment ends a scheme, and 1x is not one.
lang, id and base with a prefix other than xml are ordinary attributes.
Bad values of all three are reported and the parser still accepts the document.
A parameter-entity reference inside a markup declaration of an external parameter entity that the internal subset references: allowed (WFC PEs in Internal Subset does not apply).
The replacement text of a reference inside such a declaration ends the declaration.
The replacement text holds the opening parenthesis of a group and not the closing one.
The replacement text holds the inner bracket of a conditional section and not its other delimiters.
A conditional section whose keyword comes from a parameter entity, in an external parameter entity.
WFC PEs in Internal Subset: a reference inside a markup declaration of the internal subset.
WFC PE Between Declarations: the replacement text of a reference between declarations is not whole declarations.
A reference between declarations whose replacement text is one whole declaration.
A reference written as a character reference in an entity value reaches the internal subset inside a markup declaration of the replacement text: WFC PEs in Internal Subset.
The same nesting violation, in an external parameter entity that the external subset references.
In the external subset the reference that the character reference makes is allowed inside the declaration.
A default in the external subset that is not an AttValue (it holds a <), for an attribute the tag leaves out.

The same default, for a tag that specifies the attribute. The well-formedness constraints on an attribute value apply to the declaration whether or not a tag uses it; the parser reads the default when it supplies it, so this document is accepted.
An entity declared after a reference to a parameter entity that was not read is not processed (standalone is not yes), so the reference to it is not replaced.
The same entity declared before the reference is processed.
With standalone="yes" the declaration after the unread reference is processed.
